items.rationale: Per-server state is not shared, so each of the 4 servers enforces the full limit separately and a client can get about 4x through. State must live in shared storage such as Redis.

Each command is atomic but the read-decide-write sequence is not: another server can run commands between this server's GET and SET, so two requests can both spend the last token. A single Lua script makes the whole sequence atomic.
Refill: 2 s x 4 = 8 tokens, so 3 + 8 = 11, capped at the capacity of 8. Spending 1 leaves 7. An answer of 10 forgets the cap.

items.answer: From Redis (redis.call('TIME') inside the script), so all servers share one clock and clock skew between servers cannot hand out extra tokens
accepted: use redis TIME so all servers share one clock
from redis itself because API server clocks can differ
items.rationale: API servers' clocks differ by small unpredictable amounts; reading time inside the script gives one shared clock. Choosing the API server shows M5.
429 Too Many Requests (RFC 6585) signals the rate limit, Retry-After tells the client when to retry, and the standard error body keeps errors consistent. A 200 for a refused request is M2.
